title: Chemistry Measurement Lab Tools & Density Visual Worksheet
subtitle: Instrument choice, units, density, percent error, and evidence-based reasoning
learning_targets: Match common lab tools to the quantity and unit they measure.
Choose an appropriate tool and justify the choice with visual evidence.
Calculate density and percent error with correct units and reasonable precision.
Diagnose a measurement error and name a specific repair action.

answers.choice_1: Graduated cylinder. Its narrow shape and graduated scale support a more precise volume reading than a beaker.
answers.choice_2: Beaker. The task asks for an approximate amount and mixing space, not a precise delivered volume.
answers.photo_evidence: Any two visible features: tall/narrow vessel, graduated marks, numbered scale, stable base, or pouring lip.
answers.dataset: Set A is accurate and precise. Set B is precise but not accurate.
answers.case_claim: The result is close to the accepted value, but the student should repeat trials before judging precision.
answers.repair: Read the bottom of the meniscus at eye level, record one estimated digit, keep units through every step, and repeat measurements.
